title: Mixed-version consumer fleet and backward-incompatible schema rollout
context: A telemetry producer started emitting a 21-field configuration record. Some older strict consumers parse exactly 20 fields; others already support 21. Regions with rollout_enabled=false continue using a cached 20-field safe record, unaffected by the new producer. Rollout change is reversible and does not alter the schema itself.
semantics: sensor-NAME is locally down if rollout_enabled AND strict_schema AND expected_fields != producer_fields. A sensor with rollout_enabled=false continues to process its known-healthy cached record, regardless of expected_fields. A non-strict parser handles either version. All other nodes fail only through graph dependencies.

hypotheses.description: The east strict consumer requires exactly 20 fields.
The Linux sensor rejects fields because it is not strict.
The updated producer contract is incompatible with strict older west consumers during rollout.
All older consumers fail even when the rollout is disabled or parsing is non-strict.

actions.meaning: Globally revert producer to 20 fields, including east consumers that already expect 21
Disable rollout for west, retaining its known-healthy cached record
Deploy a validated 21-field strict parser to west

provenance: Inspired by the 2024-07-19 CrowdStrike channel update failure; these are synthetic contracts and do not reproduce CrowdStrike internals.
